Blockhold · Claude Opus 5 visual review

Built for fingers.

Clear choices, forgiving taps and a visible way out of every targeting mode. The same warm Blockhold identity, with calmer surfaces and less friction.

All seven towers, within reach.

The build picker stays in one place and fits a 667 × 375 phone. Holding an option reveals its details without moving the choices under your finger.

Selection behaves consistently.

Tap a tower, plot or hero to select it. Tap it again to dismiss. Switching to a tower or plot releases the hero, so a later tap cannot accidentally send the hero walking.

Touch tolerates a small finger roll. Near-miss foundation taps get a small allowance after exact scene hits; panning and cancelled touches never buy or select.

Aim, or cancel.

Invalid plot placement uses the same message area and keeps the credit. Ability captions make the action bar easier to recognize.

Pause and leave without hunting.

Portrait has a useful place.

The battlefield remains landscape. Rotating upright pauses play, instead of hiding a running battle. The rotation prompt offers a return to the menu that preserves an eligible solo save.

Returning to landscape leaves the game paused until you choose Resume.

Review decisions and verification

Claude Opus 5 reviewed the screenshots and input code through Claude Code. Its recommendations informed touch tolerance, cancellation, panel bounds, hierarchy and orientation handling.

Single-tap buying stays fast; destructive actions keep their confirmation. XP remaining stays visible, as requested.

347 game tests and 28 browser checks cover selection, hold-to-inspect, gesture cancellation, aiming, page reload and rotation. Device views are Chromium touch emulation; no physical iPhone testing is implied.

Design reference: Apple’s game-control guidance, including 44 × 44 pt targets for frequently used controls. The web UI uses a 44 CSS-pixel minimum for these controls.

Uses Blockhold’s existing wood, parchment, gold and blue palette. Images are actual renderer captures; account access and long planning windows are staged for review, not changes to gameplay balance.
